newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby corn ends firm on funds, soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby corn ends firm on funds, soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT nearby corn futures closed firm on Wednesday, in line with gains in soybean futures, with heavy fund buying noted, traders said.
"Funds continue to support the market," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Fundamental news was primarily bearish as commercial selling continued, suggesting farmers may be bringing corn out of storage. Cargill Inc reportedly sold 2.5 million bushels March in early dealings but then bought 1.5 March.
Farmers Commodities Corp sold one million March on the day, traders said.
Also, South Korea may spurn higher-priced U.S. supplies and instead buy 300,000 tonnes Argentine corn, a South Korea National Livestock Cooperatives Federation source said.
The source told Reuters that Argentine corn costs $109 per tonne FOB, compared with U.S. corn at $116 a tonne.

On the day, Griffin Trading bought 2.5 million March, Merrill Lynch, Dean Witter and SAK Futures each bought two million March, traders said. Tenco Inc bought one million December and sold 1.5 million March.
Corn closed one cent per bushel higher to one cent lower with March up 1/4 at $2.75.

In options, the play was in March $2.70 puts for the second straight day. Continental Grain reportedly bought 500 March $2.70 puts at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents. Refco Inc bought 100 March $2.70 puts, traders said.
Corn volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 64,502 contracts, according to CBOT data.
